findings.short_summary: Quote date is integer epoch (days since 1970-01-01), encoded as TEXT digits-only, not parseable date string
findings.summary: The spec states 'stamp with GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date' but does not specify type or encoding. The real code uses `Date` type (integer days since 1970-01-01) and the formula encodes it as `TEXT(...,"0")` — a digits-only string (e.g., "19150"), not a date string (e.g., "2024-08-01"). All A-side outputs assume the quote_date is parseable from an ISO-8601 or YYYY-MM-DD date string, which diverges from the code's integer epoch representation.
findings.description: Quote date representation: spec says 'GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date' (unspecified type); code uses `Date` (integer, epoch-relative days since 1970-01-01) and formula `=TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE(...,"tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0")`. A-side assumes string parsing (NaiveDate or DateTime<Utc>); B-side correctly identifies integer type and digits-only encoding.

findings.short_summary: Transient carry-forward preserves entire prior Mark (including original quote_date); Permanent error blocks all carry
findings.summary: The spec focuses on 'stamp with GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date' but does not explicitly address what happens when a symbol reads as Transient or Permanent on a subsequent settle pass. The code (read_marks, lines 873-883) implements: (1) Transient or absent → if prior mark exists, carry forward the entire prior Mark (preserving its original quote_date) unchanged; (2) Permanent error → degrade immediately, NO prior carry regardless of history. A-side outputs focus narrowly on mark production and omit these carry-forward and error-blocking semantics.
findings.description: Settlement carry-forward behavior: spec requirement SHEET-MARK-004 covers only mark stamping, not transient/permanent handling. Real code implements SHEET-MARK-005/006 (from B-reconstructions): Transient carries prior Mark with original quote_date (line 875); Permanent blocks carry (line 882). A-side does not address these semantics—all A outputs are narrowly focused on producing a mark from a numeric reading.

findings.short_summary: Transport failure (read_price_pass error) propagates without emitting empty MarksProduced; offline carry-forward is runtime's responsibility
findings.summary: The spec requirement SHEET-MARK-004 says nothing about transport failures or offline resilience. The code (read_marks, lines 817-822) enforces: if `read_price_pass` returns `Err`, that error is propagated and NO `MarksProduced` is returned — never an empty set that would signal 'all symbols degraded' and null live positions. Runtime's responsibility to retain its prior cached marks (with their quote-date stamps) on offline. A-side outputs do not address this failure mode.
findings.description: Transport failure handling: spec does not mention. Real code propagates errors (line 828 `client.read_price_pass()?`); test at line 132 confirms 'a transport failure must propagate, not emit empty marks'. A-side outputs are silent on this failure semantics.
